sentence: This project studies how Alzheimer’s disease splits into distinct molecular subtypes and looks for the key drivers behind each subtype.
This project studies whether epigenetic risk linked to aging identifies a vulnerable brain that is prone to delirium and cognitive decline.
This project maps the forms of transcripts made by distinct cell types in the prefrontal cortex from childhood to adulthood.
This project studies how risk genes and non-coding variants linked to schizophrenia affect neurogenesis, using brain organoids.
This project tests whether cardiac MRI can predict how well the left ventricle recovers after coronary revascularization.
This project uses computational approaches on genomics and single cell data to study how the serrated pathway of colon cancer develops.
This project builds a resource of regulatory elements in the human genome, including deep-learning models of how they work.
This project studies what recurrent mutations in a gene do in invasive lobular carcinoma of the breast, using preclinical models.
This project tests whether combining seasonal mRNA vaccines with protein or split influenza vaccines gives stronger protection, and studies the immune mechanisms.
This project develops a magnetic resonance imaging method that measures tissue pH and protein quickly, to judge how brain metastases respond to treatment.
This project studies how a protein called Neuregulin-1 protects against neuronal injury in cerebral malaria, using 3D in vitro models, animals and humans.
This project tests a drug called tazemetostat together with immunotherapy in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
This project runs a cancer research center focused on basic science discoveries that lead toward cancer therapeutics, diagnostics and devices.
This project builds a Bayesian model that corrects undercounts of children under age five in small areas across four southeastern states.
This project builds a cohort of Asian American adults to study risk factors for cancer, including stress, health behaviors and healthcare access.
This project studies how the molecules acetyl-CoA and S-adenosylmethionine affect cell signaling and metabolism in response to nutrients.
This project studies how early life immune development shapes vaccine responses and the risk of respiratory infection and asthma in infants.
This project studies how environmental stress changes the way messenger RNA is processed in a green alga called Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
This project builds computer models that predict how blood-contacting medical devices cause platelet activation and receptor shedding.
This project uses murine and human models to understand how germline gene mutations lead to acute myeloid leukemia.
